title: Bidirectional A* in Lisbon—Two Fronts, One Route!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* race from both the start and goal along real street intersections, meeting in the middle. This reel visualizes how heuristics and synchronized frontiers shrink search space on a road-graph.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ Lisbon (Alcântara) is the stage—Bidirectional A* is the strategy.

🧠 Bidirectional A* runs **two simultaneous A*** searches: one forward from the start node and one backward from the goal node. Each side expands using a priority queue ordered by:

📌 **f(n) = g(n) + h(n)** (forward) and a symmetric cost model backward.

🗺️ On a **real street map**, intersections become vertices and road segments become weighted edges—turning the city into a graph search problem. The key win: as the forward and backward frontiers grow, they **meet sooner**, cutting down unnecessary exploration compared to single-direction search.

📍In this visualization, notice how the “two waves” reduce the explored area while still guaranteeing an optimal route (given an admissible heuristic).

🚍🧩 How fast can a pathfinding search find the best route through a real city graph?

In this video, **Bidirectional A*** expands from both the start and the goal at the same time, using graph theory (intersections = nodes, streets = weighted edges) and a heuristic to guide exploration. When the two searches meet, you get the shortest path without wasting time exploring the entire map.
